answer: Sybil cost is pinned to scarce, non-transferable anchors. Each agent registers one hardware vertex it proves at runtime: a signed per-round challenge only that device can answer in time. Registration also needs a bond from a distinct human operator, slashed if a clone appears. A thousand fakes then need a thousand real devices and bonded operators, each opening a separate inlet of accountability. Detection is pooled: the wharf where identities dock is one shared bond pool, and one duplicate seizes every bond tied to that anchor, so a fake costs more than it earns.
